references.text: Pharaoh's wise men and sorcerers also tried to do the same with their secret arts, showing a pattern where Egyptian magicians attempted to imitate Moses' signs.
Egypt's magicians did the same with their secret arts, reflecting their earlier success in mimicking the plagues, unlike their failure to produce gnats.
The magicians were able to bring forth frogs with their secret arts, but here at the plague of gnats they failed for the first time.
The magicians acknowledged that this is God's finger, confirming that their magical powers had reached their limit against God's power.
The magicians could not stand before Moses because of the plague of boils, showing their continued powerlessness against God's works.
Daniel describes how no magicians, enchanters, or wise men could reveal the king's dream, demonstrating the limits of human wisdom compared to God's revelation.
Jannes and Jambres, who according to Jewish tradition were the names of Pharaoh's magicians, opposed Moses, but their folly was made plain to all, as happened with the plague of gnats.
Simon the sorcerer saw that the Spirit was given through the apostles' laying on of hands and wanted to buy this power, showing that human magic cannot imitate God's true power.
